title: Armand Piron and the sale of Shimmy Like My Sister Kate
summary: Piron was New Orleans' best violinist; Dominique and Russell agree the song was Armstrong's, bought cheaply by Piron and Clarence Williams.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well, Armand P. Ron, the best violinist right down in New Orleans, he was. And he could play jazz. Him of course. He'd play any kind of music. He was a complete musician. But one thing that you can't shake like my sister Kate, that's Louie Armstrong's number.
That's what I heard too. Louie told me that.
Louie's Armstrong's number, because P. Ron told it to me himself. And Clarence Williams told it to me himself.
Yeah. They got it away from Louie, I don't know for how much. Very cheap.
I think $25 or $50. Something like that.
I don't know. I can't tell you the price, but I'm going to tell you the price.
And they made money off of that number.
